claim: GitHub Pages is a free static-hosting service built directly into the repo that already hosts your code.
detail: Point Pages at any subdirectory of a repository and GitHub serves it over HTTPS with a built-in URL, custom domain support, and automatic deploys on every push. For a static blog the entire hosting bill is zero, with no server, no DNS glue, and no renewal dates.
steps: Pick a directory (e.g. autopilot-blog/site/) as the site source in repo Settings → Pages
Push (or let the engine push) the built HTML and the site deploys in under a minute
Optionally map a custom domain in the same settings page
source_title: GitHub Docs — About custom domains and GitHub Pages

claim: Cloudflare Pages is a free static hosting platform with a global CDN and preview deploys for every pull request.
detail: Connect a Git repo and every branch or PR gets its own preview URL, while the main branch gets a production URL on Cloudflare's network. The free tier covers static sites comfortably and custom domains are supported without a separate CDN bill.
steps: Create a Pages project in the Cloudflare dashboard and link the repo
Point the build output at the static folder
Add a custom domain in the project's domains tab

claim: Netlify's free tier hosts a static site with SSL, CI/CD from Git, forms and generous bandwidth — no card required.
detail: Netlify is the classic pick for static sites: drag a folder in or connect a repo, and it handles builds, redirects, and TLS certificates automatically. The free plan's limits are far beyond what a personal blog ever needs.

claim: is-a.dev gives you a real custom domain — username.is-a.dev — completely free, pointed at your GitHub Pages site.
detail: It is the fastest path from user.github.io/repo to a name that looks like an actual domain. You request the subdomain, add a CNAME record, and the platform handles the certificate. There is no invoice, ever.
steps: Request yourhandle.is-a.dev in the is-a.dev app
Add the provided CNAME record to your repo's Pages settings
Wait a few minutes for propagation

claim: eu.org has offered free subdomains to anyone for decades — the oldest free-domain project still around.
detail: The catch is patience: the application is manual and approval can take days to weeks, and inactive domains get reclaimed. For projects that can wait, it is a genuinely free, transferable subdomain.

claim: Static sites are cheap to host because there is no server to keep awake — which is why so many hosts give the tier away.
detail: Files are cached at edge nodes and served from memory; there is no database, no runtime, no scaling. When the marginal cost of serving a page approaches zero, hosting becomes a feature to win signups — and that is the deal a personal blog gets to keep.
